prompt: Which of the following is the lesson's second definition of a MANET?
options: A collection of fixed wireless relays forming a permanent network that is run under centralized administration and established infrastructure
A collection of wired exchanges forming a permanent backbone that relies on established infrastructure and centralized administration
A collection of satellite terminals forming a network through one central ground hub that provides the established infrastructure
A collection of low-power wireless mobile nodes forming a temporary wireless network without any established infrastructure or centralized administration
explanation: Page 11 defines a MANET as a collection of low-power wireless mobile nodes forming a temporary wireless network without established infrastructure or centralized administration.

prompt: Which feature does the lesson NOT list among the main MANET features?
options: Dedicated fixed relay towers
Quality of service for competing traffic
Frequency hopping across channels
Self-forming, self-healing connectivity
explanation: Page 12 lists self-forming and self-healing, frequency hopping, quality of service, dynamic membership and unicast, multicast and broadcast support.

prompt: Which pair of main features relates to changing membership and to network restoration, in that order?
options: Frequency hopping; quality of service
Self-forming, self-healing; unicast, multicast and broadcast support
Quality of service; dynamic number of members
Dynamic number of members; self-forming, self-healing
explanation: Page 12 lists a dynamic number of members in the net and self-forming, self-healing among the main features.

prompt: Concurrent flooding is described in the lesson as traffic that is delivered in which way?
options: Broadcast, "all informed", by parallel transmission
Sent to one recipient through a single path
Hopped across several frequencies in sequence
Routed through a central controller that sets each path
explanation: Page 17 describes concurrent flooding as traffic broadcast (all informed) by parallel transmission, so that no rebuild is needed.

prompt: Which statement describes the remote operation of the E-LynX?
options: It is available only on hand-held radios
It replicates the local operation and is IP/Ethernet based
It uses a 2.8-inch display and keypads
It is carried out through the G-10N key fill device and a data connector
explanation: Page 29 states that remote operation replicates the local operation and is IP/Ethernet based, on all radio platforms and configurations.

prompt: Which of the following describes the local operation of the E-LynX?
options: A 3.5-inch color display of 480 x 640 pixels, with keypads
A 2.8-inch monochrome display of 240 x 320 pixels, with touch keys
A 2.8-inch color display of 240 x 320 pixels, with keypads
IP/Ethernet-based screen replication from a management station
explanation: Page 29 describes local operation as a 2.8-inch color display, 240 x 320 pixels, and keypads.

prompt: Which list gives the built-in information security capabilities of all E-LynX configurations?
options: Embedded TRANSEC based on AES 128, anti-tamper and erase abilities, keys management and loading
Embedded TRANSEC based on AES 256, anti-jam hopping tables, open key distribution
Embedded TRANSEC based on AES 256, plain-text fallback, automatic key sharing
Embedded TRANSEC based on AES 256, anti-tamper and erase abilities, keys management and loading
explanation: Page 30 lists embedded TRANSEC based on AES 256, anti-tamper and erase abilities, and keys management and loading.

prompt: Which list gives the waveforms of the E-LynX shown in the lesson?
options: NB, WB, WMA-HC, STANAG 4204 and SINCGARS
NB, WB, WMA-HC, STANAG 4204 and CNR
NB, WB, WMA-HC, STANAG 5066 and CNR
NB, WB, WMA-LC, STANAG 4204 and CNR
explanation: Page 31 lists the narrowband, wideband, WMA-HC, STANAG 4204 and CNR waveforms.

prompt: For connectors, the visual inspection looks for which conditions?
options: Damage, corrosion, and broken or bent pins
Fraying, cuts and broken insulation
Cracks and any other external damage
Rough action and interference in the buttons
explanation: Page 25 lists damage, corrosion and broken or bent pins for connectors, while cable inspection covers fraying, cuts and broken insulation.

prompt: Which step of the four-step fault procedure comes immediately before fault repair?
options: Fault identification
Fault isolation
Fault verification (including BIT)
Preventive inspection
explanation: Page 27 shows the order fault identification, fault isolation, fault repair, repair verification.

prompt: On the VS50-VA indicator lights, what does the CALL light on orange show?
options: The radio is transmitting voice
A technical fault from a built-in test error
The radio is receiving voice, only when squelch is detected
PBIT and IBIT are in progress
explanation: Page 50 states that CALL on orange means the radio is receiving voice, only when squelch is detected.

prompt: Which statement correctly contrasts the E-LynX hand-held radio with the VS50-VA vehicular adapter?
options: The hand-held has 5 W output power; the VS50-VA has 50 W
The hand-held has 50 W output power; the VS50-VA has 5 W
Both have 5 W output power
Both have 50 W output power
explanation: Pages 38 and 46 give 5 W for the hand-held radio and 50 W for the VS50-VA.

prompt: Which Nodes Information parameter shows the received signal strength?
options: SNR
Dist
D.Rate
RSSI
explanation: Page 56 describes RSSI as received signal strength, while SNR measures received signal quality.

prompt: Which statement about the ping option is correct?
options: It stays enabled permanently once it is first activated
It is available only at the secure level
It must be re-enabled every time the device is turned on or off
It can check another E-LynX radio but never an IP host
explanation: Page 66 states that ping must be re-enabled each time the device is turned on or off; page 54 states it can check a radio or an IP host.

prompt: In Net Performance, what does the Dest field specify?
options: The size of the packets to send
The pause time between each packet sending
The remote ID that the packet is sent to
The number of packets received at the destination
explanation: Page 67 describes Dest as the remote ID that the packet is sent to.

prompt: Which statement describes the Node ID?
options: A shared parameter used by all transceivers in the net
A unique configuration parameter given to each transceiver
The management IP used for management purposes
The technician address used to access the radio from a computer terminal
explanation: Page 68 describes the node ID as a unique configuration parameter given to each transceiver.

prompt: Which services does the lesson list under data, positions and video integration?
options: Location, voice and data
Data, voice and video
Location, data and video
Location, voice and video
explanation: Page 72 lists location, data and video for the data, positions and video integration.

prompt: Which Integrator best practice prevents traffic from crossing into networks it should not reach?
options: Reduce traffic on the network
Deny traffic leaking
Security of the integrated services
Dynamic routing between the networks
explanation: Page 70 lists deny traffic leaking among the best practices of the Integrator.

prompt: Which list gives the services shown on the Integrator slide between H.Q., C.P. and field units?
options: Location, voice, data and imagery
Voice, data, video and telemetry
Location, voice, text and video
Location, voice, data and video
explanation: Page 69 lists location, voice, data and video among the services of the Integrator.

prompt: Which of the following can be viewed through the Test menu?
options: The elapsed time counter
The operator password
The Node ID assigned by the operator
The group voice names
explanation: Page 58 lists testing the RX and TX paths, software and hardware versions, network performance and the elapsed time counter.
